howDoI.q: How do I make a block that launches rockets by itself?
How do I make a rocket burst at the top of its flight?
How do I keep two launchers from firing at the same time?
How do I let my hero launch a firework with a key?
How do I make a burst bigger than one block?
How do I make a firework that goes off again and again?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Fireworks Night is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. This one is about fireworks drawn with monsters: a rocket is a monster on a path up, and when its path ends it turns into another monster, its burst. It has two short levels. Level 1 has two launchers and lets you launch a rocket of your own. Level 2 is a show of big bursts over a sleeping town. Each takes a minute or two.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

The Left and Right arrows walk, Space jumps and Enter launches a rocket. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Nothing in this game can hurt you. For a sky that twinkles by itself, see Twinkle, Twinkle; for monsters that keep a shape, Birds of a Feather.

pages.head: Level 1: Launch!
pages.html:
Level 1: Launch!

You start on a little mound in a night field. LAUNCHERS ARE BLOCKS THAT MAKE ROCKETS stands below it. Past it is a launcher with a pink band: every few seconds a rocket climbs out of it, slows near the top and bursts: a small pink spray of sparks that falls a little as it fades. AT THE TOP THE ROCKET TURNS INTO A BURST stands beside it. A second launcher, with a teal band, has its own rhythm, and EACH LAUNCHER KEEPS ITS OWN TIME stands past it. At PRESS ENTER TO LAUNCH ONE, press Enter: Nova swings an arm and a rocket of their own goes up from them and bursts over their head. The door is at the end.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A launcher is a block. Open fw.bbl in the blocks editor and pick launch.pink. In its Time section, the monster it gives birth to is the pink rocket, every 70 ticks: a little under four seconds at 18.2 ticks a second. The rocket is born in the launcher's own square, so there is nothing to place for it. A launcher only gives birth while it is on the screen or close to it.
  • The rocket is a monster on a path. Open fw.mon in the monsters editor and pick the pink rocket. Its path goes straight up five blocks in three parts, each with its own Speed (pixels per tick): 12, then 4, then 2, so it shoots out of the tube and slows near the top. Its two pictures in fw.mbl take turns every 2 ticks, so the sparks of its trail fizz.
  • The burst. The rocket's Lives is Until the end of its path, and its When destroyed it becomes is the pink burst. So at the top of the climb, in the same square, the rocket is gone and the burst is there. The burst is one block: six pictures from a white flash to a ring of sparks to a few dim embers, each shown for a few ticks. Its own path falls one block at a speed of 1, so it sinks a little as it fades.
  • Gone for good. The burst's Lives is Until the end of its path too, and it becomes nothing, so when it has fallen its block it is gone. Nothing is left over to fill up the sky.
  • Two clocks. launch.teal is a second block with the same picture and a teal band, giving birth to the teal rocket every 97 ticks. The time belongs to the block, not to the square, so two launchers with their own rhythm have to be two blocks. With 70 and 97 ticks they go up together only once every 6,790 ticks, about six minutes.
  • Enter. Open hero.chr in the character editor. The Throw sequence has Enter as its key and, in the middle of the arm swing, a frame whose picture is the pink rocket: a frame like that gives birth to the monster instead of showing a picture. It is born in the square of Nova's head and flies the same path up from there. The rising whoosh is the sequence's sound.

pages.head: Level 2: The Big Show
pages.html:
Level 2: The Big Show

The field runs along the edge of a sleeping town, a few windows still lit. 9 MONSTERS IN STEP MAKE 1 BIG BURST stands at the start. Over three wide mortars go three big fireworks, each three blocks across: a red ring with a gold ring inside it, a green and gold peony, and a gold willow whose sparks droop as they burn out. Each one goes up again a few seconds after it fades, for as long as you stay. THE BURST TURNS BACK INTO ITS ROCKET and RING, PEONY, WILLOW: NEW PICTURES, ONE TRICK stand between them, with a pink and a teal launcher from level 1. The door is past the willow.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Nine monsters in a square. A monster picture is one block, 20 pixels. A burst three blocks across is nine monsters: open two.map and over each mortar you will see nine of them placed in a square, each with its own pictures, the part of the burst it shows. They all have the same path at the same speeds, so they move as one and never come apart (the same trick that keeps a flock in a V).
  • Mirrors. The monster file holds only 100 pictures, and three big bursts of five or six frames would need about 150. A burst is the same on the left and the right, so the right-hand blocks show the left-hand pictures Mirrored: in the monsters editor, each corner of a path has a picture direction. The ring and the peony are also the same at the top and the bottom, so their bottom blocks are Flipped, and the bottom right one Upside down. Four pictures draw a whole frame of the ring.
  • A firework that never stops. These monsters are not born by a launcher; they are placed on the map and live for ever, by taking turns. Each block is two monsters. The flight drops to the mortar, waits by going on down into the ground and back up (with a clear picture, so you see nothing), then climbs. Its Lives is Until the end of its path and it becomes the burst. The burst falls two blocks as it fades, and it becomes the flight again. Only the middle block's flight shows the rocket.
  • Its own time. The ring's flight goes 2 blocks down under its mortar and back up at a speed of 2, the peony's 3 blocks, the willow's 5 blocks at a speed of 4, so each takes its own time round and they rarely go off together.
  • Falling. The ring and the peony fall by their path: one block at a speed of 1, then one at a speed of 2, faster and faster like anything dropped. The willow stays put and falls inside its own pictures instead: its sparks droop and trail, so it is mirrored only left to right and needs six pictures a frame. It lives for a set time (47 ticks) instead.
  • The town. Six blocks, house.wall to house.chimney, a few dark blue-gray walls and roofs with warm windows, stacked into houses. They are in the air, like the sky, so Nova walks in front of them.
  • More sky in view. The screen follows Nova up or down only once they are 60 pixels from its middle. Both levels start them on a mound two blocks high, so when they step down to the field the screen stays where it was, and two more rows of sky stay in view.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It has no particles. A spark cannot be its own thing that flies and falls. Each frame of a burst is a picture of all its sparks at one moment, drawn ahead of time. A burst only moves as smoothly as the frames you draw.
  • It cannot fade. There are no see-through colors. A spark fades by being drawn in darker colors, frame by frame, and goes out by not being drawn.
  • It has no random. Every ring goes off the same way every time. Different times and different bursts make a show feel random.
  • A burst cannot make a sound. A monster plays no sound when it turns into another, and a launcher plays none when it gives birth. Only Nova's own launch has a whoosh.
  • A monster picture is one block. Anything bigger is several monsters on one path, and the file holds 64 monsters and 100 pictures. This game uses 58 monsters and most of the pictures.
  • Flashes must stay small. A burst begins with a small white flash, a few pixels, never a bright screen. Fast, big flashes can hurt some players' eyes, so a show keeps them small and spaced out (see Flash Safe).

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In fw.bbl, change launch.pink's every ticks from 70 to 30 and watch a busy launcher.
  • In fw.mon, make the pink rocket's path climb two more blocks. Its burst follows it up.
  • Change the pink burst's When destroyed it becomes to the teal rocket, and one firework sets off the next.
  • Draw a burst of your own in fw.mbl: a frame is a picture of every spark at one moment, a little farther out and a little darker each time.
  • Give the ring's flight a longer wait, and see the show change its rhythm.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
